# Copy-ready prompts

## Install or upgrade this agent

Install Go-To-Market for Orgo from
https://github.com/jbellsolutions/go-to-market-orgo on the computer I
give you. Read AGENTS.md, START-HERE.md, llms.txt, and the Orgo llms.txt index
before changing anything. Do all technical work yourself. First inspect for an
existing deployment and preserve its credentials, configuration, conversations,
memory, vault, connected channels, and customizations. Use the repository's
pinned release and installer. Connect existing Slack, Telegram, Honcho,
Latitude, calendar, proposal, CRM, and other approved tools when the credentials
already exist. Keep Agent Bundle disabled. Keep dashboard and A2A private unless
authenticated remote access is explicitly required. Ask me only for a missing
secret or external authorization, one item at a time. Run static, runtime,
channel, A2A-auth, memory, observability, and permission-stop tests. Roll back if
verification fails. Finish with the version, health evidence, connected and
intentionally unconnected services, preserved data, and rollback point.

## Pair it with another agent

Connect this Go-To-Market for Orgo agent to the agent I name using authenticated
A2A. Inspect both agents first. Create separate per-peer tokens, keep them in the
private credential stores, use a private network address, and allowlist only the
authenticated peer names. Enable outbound A2A for normal human-facing sessions,
but keep inbound A2A on the reduced toolset with no terminal, external send,
approval, credential, or recursive A2A authority. Test Agent Card discovery and
one harmless request in both directions. Then test that an A2A request cannot
approve a send, spend, permission change, credential transfer, production
change, or persistent worker.

## Update safely

Update Go-To-Market for Orgo from its canonical repository. Record the
current commit, image, health, state counts, and rollback location. Stage and
test the candidate first. Apply only managed files and preserve the private
.env, OAuth material, config, databases, conversations, Honcho state, vault,
and user customizations. Verify Hermes, Slack/Telegram, Honcho, Latitude, A2A,
Agent Factory, and permission stops. If any required check fails, restore the
previous managed release without replacing state databases.
